visuals.title: Where AIDS complications hit
visuals.text: PCP in the lungs, toxoplasma and cryptococcus in the brain, CMV in the eyes, candida in the oesophagus, HIVAN in the kidneys, Kaposi's in the skin.

glossary.Maculopapular rash: A rash of flat red patches (macules) mixed with small raised bumps (papules).
glossary.Mucosal ulcers: Painful breaks in the lining of the mouth, genitals or other moist surfaces.
glossary.Opportunistic infection: An infection by an organism that normally causes little harm but causes disease when the immune system is weak.
glossary.Night sweats: Drenching sweating during sleep, often a sign of infection, TB or lymphoma.
glossary.Non-productive cough: A dry cough that brings up no sputum.
glossary.Cryptococcus: A fungus (Cryptococcus neoformans) inhaled from soil and bird droppings that can spread to the meninges in immunosuppression.
glossary.Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopat: A brain infection by JC virus that destroys myelin in several areas, seen with severe immunosuppression.
glossary.Collapsing FSGS: An aggressive form of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis where glomerular capillaries collapse; typical of HIVAN.
glossary.Nephrotic syndrome: Heavy proteinuria, low albumin and oedema caused by leaky glomeruli.
glossary.EBV: Epstein-Barr virus, a herpesvirus that causes glandular fever and drives some lymphomas.
glossary.Hodgkin's lymphoma: A lymph node cancer containing Reed-Sternberg cells.
glossary.Burkitt's lymphoma: A very fast-growing B-cell lymphoma linked to EBV and HIV.
glossary.Molluscum contagiosum: A poxvirus skin infection causing small pearly umbilicated bumps, extensive in HIV.
glossary.Antigen/antibody combined test: A blood test detecting both HIV p24 antigen and anti-HIV antibodies, shortening the window period.
glossary.Confirmatory assay: A second, different test used to confirm a positive screening result.
glossary.Antenatal booking: The first full pregnancy appointment, usually around 8 to 12 weeks, when screening bloods are taken.
glossary.Finger-prick sample: A drop of capillary blood taken by pricking the fingertip.
glossary.HIV RNA PCR: A test that amplifies and counts HIV genetic material in the blood to give the viral load.
glossary.Hepatitis screen: Blood tests for hepatitis B and C infection.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes, a blood test of kidney function and salts.
glossary.Septicaemia: Bacteria multiplying in the bloodstream causing systemic illness.
glossary.Stool microbiology: Lab testing of a stool sample for bacteria, parasites and viruses.
glossary.Tenofovir DF: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, an NRTI used in HIV treatment and prevention.
glossary.Emtricitabine: An NRTI often paired with tenofovir as the cART backbone.
glossary.Abacavir: An NRTI; check HLA-B*5701 first because of hypersensitivity risk.
glossary.Lamivudine: An NRTI used in HIV and hepatitis B.
glossary.Atazanavir: A protease inhibitor, usually boosted with ritonavir.
glossary.Ritonavir: A protease inhibitor used in low doses to boost levels of other protease inhibitors.
glossary.Triple therapy: Three antiretrovirals together: two NRTIs plus a third agent.
glossary.OI prophylaxis: Preventive medicine given to stop opportunistic infections when CD4 is low.
glossary.Non-live vaccines: Vaccines with no living organism, safe in immunosuppression; live vaccines can cause infection.
glossary.Ischaemic stroke: Stroke caused by a blocked artery to the brain.
glossary.Haemorrhagic stroke: Stroke caused by bleeding into or around the brain.
glossary.Toxic epidermal necrolysis: A severe drug reaction where large areas of skin blister and peel off.
glossary.Drug-induced lupus: A lupus-like illness caused by a medicine that settles when the drug stops.
glossary.Whole-brain irradiation: Radiotherapy given to the whole brain.
glossary.Adherence: How well a patient takes their medicines as prescribed.
glossary.Virion: A complete virus particle outside a cell.
glossary.T-helper lymphocyte: A CD4+ T cell that coordinates the immune response by activating other immune cells.
glossary.Cell-mediated immunity: Immunity carried out by T cells killing infected cells.
glossary.Humoral immunity: Immunity carried out by antibodies made by B cells.
glossary.Spindle cells: Long, thin cells; in Kaposi's sarcoma they come from endothelium.
glossary.Endothelial: Relating to the cells lining blood and lymph vessels.
glossary.Subclinical infection: An infection present but causing no symptoms.
